reading.body:
Captions offers AI video editing with eye contact correction, dubbing, and likeness manipulation features, positioning these as consent-managed tools rather than uncontrolled synthetic media.

The company operates in a space where video generation capability has outpaced legal frameworks. Eye contact correction and digital likeness creation are computationally straightforward once trained on video data, but their deployment involves consent and identity questions that law has not yet fully resolved. New York's 311 law exposure entries suggest regulatory attention, though the data does not specify whether these are proposed bills, existing statutes, or cases.

For AI infrastructure, this matters because video tools sit at the intersection of compute demand and legal constraint. Rendering edited video and training models for likeness manipulation require significant processing. If regulation tightens around synthetic media, it may shift not whether these tools exist, but where they run and who can access their models. The data does not clarify Captions' training or inference infrastructure, so it cannot speak to compute or power requirements directly.

The consent framing in the product notes is notable. It suggests the company has chosen a regulatory posture rather than a technical one, making human approval a feature rather than a barrier. This does not tell us whether that approach will survive legal scrutiny in New York or elsewhere.

profile_text.body:
Captions is an AI video generator and editor, according to its own site, aimed at turning an idea into ready-to-share content without advanced editing skills. The company was founded in 2021 and is headquartered in New York City, NY, US. It describes its editor as editing "with taste, not just speed," tailoring cuts to a user's footage while leaving details changeable, and it says the AI can edit an entire video at once by picking a style, cutting scenes and overlaying B-roll. The site also lists auto-generated captions and translated subtitles, an AI twin or digital avatars that can be reused across videos and altered by prompt, and tools it names as an ad generator, AI video editor, AI video generator, clone yourself, prompt to video, script to video, text-based video editor and transition editor. Target uses it names include short-form social videos, ads, AI UGC, faceless content, AI voiceovers, product demos, real estate listing videos, talking head videos, thought leadership and tutorials.

The product tracked for the company is Captions AI, in the video generation and editing category, noted for AI video editing, eye contact correction, dubbing and likeness manipulation consent. The company positions itself as a fast alternative to traditional editors, claiming studio-quality results in minutes and accessibility for creators regardless of expertise.

On the legal side, no cases are recorded for Captions, but law exposure is listed for New York with a count of 356. No MCP server is recorded for the company.
